## [2026-11-20](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-20.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26423>)

Seer guides a frozen research agent by predicting candidate tool responses and scoring the resulting imagined histories with two shared learned models. Only the chosen action is executed and only real responses enter the continuing history, improving several small-agent question-answering results without making real tool calls for discarded alternatives. The extra models and candidate evaluation consume computation, and the study does not establish on-device latency or memory savings.

**Limitations:** The shared decision models add a9Bbase plus adapters/head to the agent, with no measured hardware latency, peak memory, energy or training-cost accounting. Real visit extraction uses a shared external Qwen3.5-397B-A17Bservice, so the overall pipeline is not a fully local private deployment; tool-call counts do not measure its dollar/token cost. Adding simulator predictions at width4 lowers accuracy for six of eight agents compared with executing all four alternatives; width32 is below the best tested width in14of40settings. Simulator and scorer errors can overvalue bad actions, and wider search is not universally better. Training filters unfinished/error trajectories from value supervision, question-disjoint splits do not prove full semantic decontamination, and the paper does not report repeated-seed uncertainty for the main accuracy comparisons. Only Qwen/Gemma, two tool schemas and answer correctness are tested; full report quality, robust citations, context compression and broader tool/schema transfer remain unvalidated. ## [2026-11-19](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-19.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23509>)

GRAFT gives an evolutionary agent-program designer bounded examples of each parent’s successes and failures, alongside its code and aggregate fitness. Controlled searches improve held-out performance when this evidence is added, offering a way to turn evaluation logs into architectural changes without extra task executions to collect that feedback. Some gains reflect interface normalization, and the study does not establish long-horizon transfer or equal total inference cost.

**Limitations:** The authors identify MGSM language/output-interface normalization as an important source of improvement, rather than establishing a pure reasoning gain. Main model prose and the actual executor table disagree on one executor name; no claim here relies on that name. ## [2026-11-11](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-11.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14492>)

ReTrace extracts action conditions and input sources from a standard operating procedure and logged agent reasoning, then compiles them into reusable workflows whose steps are selected by code. This can remove repeated planning calls from stable, high-volume procedures while still allowing model-backed tools; on the authors’ telecom-only evaluation, execution averages 1.3 seconds versus 170 seconds for their agent. The speed–quality tradeoff remains visible: unrepaired task success is 75.8% versus 80.6%, and the recovered conditions are not formally verified.

The public telecom solo-mode study uses 74 training / 40 test inputs, successful Sonnet 4.6 traces and training-only configuration selection; eight admitted SOP-Bench domains provide a separate test. The original November 11 cs.AI entry plus the official Eastern-US schedule infer November 11 01:00 UTC paper availability; the November 10 receipt date is retained.

**Limitations:** These modified benchmark settings are not directly comparable to published leaderboard scores. Public candidate selection favors ReTrace; its advantage over few-shot on the 40 telecom test inputs is not statistically resolved, and unrepaired ReTrace trails few-shot on SOP-Bench. Repair receives training labels on SOP-Bench, where repaired zero-shot scores higher. Private enterprise completion is imperfect, construction counts are lower bounds, and changed procedures can require recompilation. No author implementation was verified or experiment reproduced.

## [2026-10-16](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-16.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22367>)

This framework evolves Python circuit generators with parallel algorithm families, a diverse program archive, and an independent evaluator that checks correctness before scoring quantum resource costs. It provides a concrete example of evaluator-guided agents discovering new algorithmic structures, rather than only refining a fixed implementation.

**Published:** 2026-10-15 · **First seen:** 2026-10-17T10:06:03.000Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Scientific Discovery, Evolutionary Search, Verification

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22367>) · [Blog](<https://www.anthropic.com/research/designing-efficient-quantum-circuits>) · [Code](<https://github.com/andigu/uncompute>) · [Project](<https://andigu.github.io/projects/uncompute/>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Methods, Figure 1 and Table 1 describe fresh agent sessions, MAP-Elites retention and eight task-specific evaluations. The Reed–Solomon decoder uses about 440,000 Toffolis and 1,837 qubits versus 5.1 million and 1,938 for its reconstructed baseline. Author circuits, evaluators and Lean proofs are available.

**Limitations:** These are simulated logical resource counts, not hardware runtime or a general agent leaderboard. Some tasks permit distribution-specific failures; sampled validation is not a universal proof. The Hermitian comparator is a naive construction, not a prior published reversible circuit. No independent reproduction.

## [2026-10-11](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-11.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Plan-and-Patch: Diffusion Language Models for Agentic Planning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10786>)

Plan-and-Patch trains a diffusion model to generate structured agent plans and replace selected spans while preserving the surrounding steps. This makes local plan revision explicit and reduces planner-generation latency in two tested environments, while showing that finding the right repair region remains a bottleneck.

**Published:** 2026-10-07 · **First seen:** 2026-10-10T10:09:23Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Agent Planning, Diffusion Models, Plan Repair

**Public availability:** 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10786>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery from the October 9 NEW batch, item 7; v1 received October 7 at 18:45:45 UTC. Appendix A.2 reports generation latency of 14.3 versus 23.3 seconds on ALFWorld and 21.7 versus 40.2 seconds on TextCraft, with diffusion versus autoregressive 8B planners and a common Qwen3-8B executor.

**Limitations:** Latency is synchronized, unbatched bf16 planner decoding on one A100, excluding environment execution. Interactive success does not consistently favor diffusion; repair restarts from the initial state. One fine-tuning seed and different pretrained model families limit attribution. No author implementation was verified; results were not reproduced.

## [2026-10-10](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-10.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12086>)

EvoAlloc learns when a program-search agent should spend resources evaluating a candidate, revising its allocation rules as results accumulate. Occasionally testing rejected candidates reveals missed opportunities, helping the search reach useful solutions with fewer evaluations.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629>)

ReAct alternates reasoning, environment actions, and observations so an agent can revise its plan using external evidence. It remains a useful foundation for tool-using agent loops because task execution and information gathering become part of the reasoning process.

**Published:** 2022-10-06 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Planning, Tool Use, Grounding

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629>) · [Project](<https://react-lm.github.io/>) · [Code](<https://github.com/ysymyth/ReAct>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The ICLR camera-ready paper compares reasoning-only, acting-only and interleaved policies on question answering, fact verification and interactive tasks; its ablations and failure analysis make the control pattern inspectable. The arXiv history records v1 on October 6, 2022 and v3 on March 10, 2023.

**Limitations:** This is a foundational method, not a claim of current benchmark leadership. Retrieval failures and repetitive loops remain possible; ReAct alone trails chain-of-thought on the reported HotpotQA setting.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147>)

This work separates task execution from a controller that assesses accumulated work, proposes next steps, evaluates their value, and dispatches workers using persistent artifact memory. It offers a way to spend larger inference budgets more effectively on long tasks by choosing which partial results to reuse, repair, or abandon.

**Published:** 2026-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Planning, Test-Time Scaling, Memory, Long-Horizon

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3, 5 and 6 provide the controller design and matched-worker comparisons across four benchmarks and three models; reported ProgramBench performance is 71.5% with GPT-5.5 versus 58.0% for Codex. Submission history verifies September 29, 2026 at 17:57:25 UTC.

**Limitations:** A new preprint with no independent reproduction here. Equal model-call allowances do not equal token, latency or FLOP budgets; control overhead hurts at small budgets, and the design underperforms direct control on the LongCoT-mini chess subset.
